Prevention: Resistant hybrids may be available, information is available from research centres and suppliers.
Use certified or clean seed from disease-free plants; this is important as this disease can be transmitted by the seeds.
Remove other susceptable host plants such as grasses which may harbour the disease.
Burn plant residues after harvesting and immediately deep plough the field as the fungus can survive on crop residues.
Rotate sorghum on a 2 year basis with crops other than cereals such as chickpeas or beans.
In poorly rotated fields, plough under infested residues where soil erosion is not a problem.
Monitoring: Monitor the crop from the seedling stage to maturity weekly for signs of disease on the leaves, stalks and the seed panicles.
Look for small circular red/orange lesions with distinct margins on the upper portion of the stalks, leaves and seeds.
The lesions can measure 2mm-2cm and can contain dark brown fungal structures.
Brown sunken areas can also appear on the stems.
When the first symptoms of the disease are seen, take direct action and remove infected plants.
Direct Control: Remove and dispose of infected plants at the earliest stage possible by burning or burying.

Chemical control is not economical for small holder farmers.
